The audit rule flags run_command's subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True) because the argv is a variable, and utils.py doesn't change, so it matches by construction (design Expected rescan results, R7 utils.py). Callers in user_group_management_utils.py and filesystem_management_utils.py build the argv with no shell, and its externally influenced operands are checked first. Path operands go through confine_dda_path (src/backend/utils/dda_user_management_utils.py:77), which update_dda_user_file_permissions (line 106) and create_dda_user_directory (line 121) apply: the resolved path must lie strictly below /aws_dda and outside /aws_dda/greengrass and /aws_dda/system, and a Folder image source outside that area gets HTTP 400 (image_source_accessor.py:441-446). uid and gid values must be 1 to 10 decimal digits (_require_posix_id, src/backend/utils/user_group_management_utils.py:60, fullmatch of _POSIX_ID_RE at line 46, applied at lines 108 and 183); user and group names are allowlisted (_require_posix_name, line 49), and path operands follow a '--' sentinel (filesystem_management_utils.py:73-95). Requirements 7.2, 7.3. No marker or suppression is added (owner decision: no suppressions, Requirement 18.4).

The audit rule flags any subprocess call whose argv isn't a literal, so it matches the fixed code by construction (design Expected rescan results, R7 python_bridge.py). The argv is [self._python_executable, '-c', RUNNER_SOURCE, self._handler_path] with no shell (lines 1043-1045): the interpreter is sys.executable (line 997; the production builders pass none), RUNNER_SOURCE is a module constant, and the handler path is positional after -c, so it is never an interpreter option. The handler path is the one externally influenced argument: _artifact_handler_path (src/backend/workflow_engine/python_bridge.py:1452), which build_bridges (line 1488) and build_producer_bridge (line 1559) use, requires its realpath to lie strictly inside the component artifact directory's realpath, so an absolute path, a '..' segment or a symlink is refused with CustomPythonNodeError before any process starts (Requirement 7.2). No marker or suppression is added (owner decision: no suppressions, Requirement 18.4).
